title: Reporting Windows and Written Reports by HomeCare Program
content:
Under the Calloway Limited Home Warranty, three program terms govern how and when a homeowner reports an item: the cosmetic report window, the late-report grace and the written-report requirement.

**Terms.**
1. *Cosmetic report window* — the calendar days after the coverage start date within which a cosmetic surface item that is not on the orientation list may still be reported. A window of 0 days means only items on the orientation list are accepted as cosmetic items.
2. *Late-report grace* — the calendar days after the end of a coverage period within which an item first noticed before the end of that period may still be reported in writing.
3. *Written report* — where the program requires it, non-emergency items must be reported in writing, through the homeowner portal or by email; a telephone report is accepted for emergencies only.

| Program | Cosmetic report window (calendar days) | Late-report grace (calendar days) | Written report required for non-emergency items |
|---|---|---|---|
| HomeCare 1-2-10 Standard | 0 | 0 | Yes |
| HomeCare 1-2-10 Select | 0 | 0 | Yes |
| HomeCare 1-3-10 Plus | 30 | 0 | Yes |
| HomeCare 2-3-10 Preferred | 30 | 7 | Yes |
| HomeCare 2-5-10 Premier | 60 | 14 | Yes |
| HomeCare 2-5-15 Reserve | 60 | 30 | Yes |

**Points of reading.**
- Every program requires written reports for non-emergency items; no program accepts a non-emergency item by telephone alone.
- The two lowest programs carry neither a cosmetic report window nor a late-report grace, so for them a cosmetic surface item is accepted only from the orientation list, and no grace days follow the end of a coverage period.
- Hypothetical illustration: under HomeCare 2-5-10 Premier, an item first noticed before its coverage period ended may still be reported in writing during the 14 calendar days after that end.
